title: The dark and light sides of dynorphin and enkephalin: from reward to aversion
title_zh: 内啡肽原肽和脑啡肽的光明与黑暗面：从奖赏到厌恶
abstract: The endogenous opioid system regulates reward and aversion through multiple peptides and receptor subtypes distributed across the brain. In this review, we focus on two opioids: enkephalins, classically linked to reward, and dynorphins, classically linked to aversion. We argue that this dichotomy oversimplifies a system defined by circuit specificity and context dependence. Methodological advances have enabled direct measurement and manipulation of endogenous opioid signaling in vivo at behaviorally relevant timescales, and evidence shows that endogenous opioid signaling is temporally dynamic, circuit-specific, and functionally heterogeneous, challenging simple reward-versus-aversion models. We discuss how these advances reshape our understanding of dynorphin and enkephalin function, using the nucleus accumbens-ventral pallidum-ventral tegmental area circuit as a framework, given its dense, interacting opioid systems and a central role in rewarding and aversive behaviors.
